situation (example wording): "Robbery rate in Memphis by month in 2025", "murder rate in Chicago in June 2025" (a rate for one month, or month by month)
what the app does today: Declined: a Current Trends rate was given only for a total of two or more months (design note, decision B), and NIBRS rates only by year.
proposed behavior: A monthly rate is that month's count per 100,000 of the population, not annualized, labeled as a rate for the month. The population is the month's own in Current Trends; before Current Trends' months begin, and in NIBRS, the agency's population for that month's year as the FBI or Crime Index publishes it. A clearance rate is still given for a whole year, not month by month.
exact default or choices offered: Each month's count per 100,000; not annualized; labeled "per 100,000 for the month".
why: Monthly rates were asked for and the data has the counts and the populations; a month's rate must never read as a yearly one.
status: Decided 2026-11-06 (Jeff: "Now" on monthly or rolling rates; the single-month rule dropped)
test cases: Tests that cite this row: scripts/test-nibrs-current.ts, scripts/test-nibrs-shadow.ts.
